name: Miami
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Miami: Latin American counterparty diligence, real estate ownership, trade finance and asset research.
hero_lede: Miami is the main US business gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, with large trade, logistics, real estate and cross-border finance activity. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for Miami matters, using public records and coordinating Florida-licensed investigators and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Miami is the county seat of Miami-Dade County, which had about 2.8 million residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate and the largest county economy in Florida. More than half of residents were born abroad, and the Greater Miami Chamber of Commerce describes the county as the largest US gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean. Trade and logistics, professional services, health care, hospitality, construction and finance lead employment. Miami International Airport is the leading US airport for international freight, and PortMiami handles about 1.2 million container units a year alongside one of the world's busiest cruise operations. Many multinationals run their Latin American regional offices from the area.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Miami because money, goods and people from across the hemisphere pass through it. A distributor in Doral may front for owners in Venezuela, Colombia or Brazil; a condominium in Brickell may be held by a Florida LLC whose members sit offshore; an exporter shipping through Miami International Airport may be part of a trade-based scheme. Lenders, insurers, acquirers and litigators need to know who controls these structures and whether assets or histories have been concealed. The work often requires Spanish and Portuguese sources and attention to Florida's licensing and recording rules.

matters.title: Latin American counterparty diligence
matters.text: Miami entities often front for owners and businesses in Latin America. We connect Florida corporate filings with registries, court records and media in the owners' home countries, in Spanish and Portuguese, to identify who controls a counterparty and whether politically exposed persons or prior enforcement are involved.

matters.title: Real estate held through entities
matters.text: Luxury condominiums and commercial property in Miami are frequently bought through limited liability companies and trusts. We work from Miami-Dade property and recording data, entity filings and litigation to trace likely beneficial owners and the strength of each attribution for lenders, litigators and compliance teams.

matters.title: Trade and freight forwarding risk
matters.text: Exporters and freight forwarders around the airport and Doral handle electronics, aircraft parts and consumer goods bound for Latin America. We review ownership, related companies, export enforcement history and trading patterns to test for misdescription, diversion or trade-based money laundering indicators.

matters.title: Asset research for judgment enforcement
matters.text: Debtors with ties to Miami may hold property, vessels, aircraft and companies across Florida and abroad. We map these from public records so counsel can plan enforcement and recognition steps, bearing in mind Florida's generous homestead protection when assessing which assets are reachable.

matters.title: Insurance and health care fraud support
matters.text: Miami-Dade has seen repeated federal and state enforcement involving health care billing and insurance claims. We support insurers and counsel with research into providers, clinic ownership, related entities and individuals' business histories, scoped to the claim and to Florida rules on investigative activity.

local_context.title: Courts in Miami
local_context.text: State civil and commercial cases in Miami-Dade are heard by the Circuit Court of the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, which runs a complex business litigation section for larger commercial disputes. Federal cases, including fraud, money laundering, sanctions and international commercial matters, are heard by the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, whose main courthouse is in Miami. Counsel decides the forum; we scope research to that court's rules.

local_context.title: International arbitration activity
local_context.text: Miami is a frequent seat for international arbitration involving Latin American parties, and international institutions hold hearings and conferences there. Florida has adopted an international commercial arbitration statute based on the UNCITRAL Model Law. Parties choose the institution and seat in their contracts; we support counsel with party background and asset research tailored to the arbitral rules and to later enforcement in Florida or abroad.

local_context.title: Florida investigator licensing
local_context.text: Florida licenses private investigation under Chapter 493, Florida Statutes, administered by the Division of Licensing of the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, which has a Miami-Dade regional office. Agencies need a Class A licence and individual investigators a Class C licence. Attorneys in the regular practice of law are exempt. Licensees may not divulge investigative file contents except to the client or as the law allows. TDSC coordinates Florida-licensed professionals for any fieldwork.

local_context.title: County government and records
local_context.text: Since 1957 Miami-Dade has operated a two-tier system: cities provide police, fire and zoning, while the county runs airports, seaports and other metropolitan services. The Clerk of the Circuit Court is an independently elected office that maintains court records and official records, including recorded property documents. Florida's broad public records laws make many local government records accessible, though court document access varies by case type.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Miami and works on Miami matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client's counsel first, whether federal litigation in the Southern District, a Miami-Dade circuit court dispute, arbitration, enforcement, or a transaction, and scope the research to it. Sources include Miami-Dade court and official records, Florida entity filings, federal dockets and enforcement releases, and registries and media in the Latin American countries connected to the matter. Any fieldwork in Florida is carried out by Florida-licensed investigators and planned around the state's consent requirement for recording conversations. Reports state sources and confidence levels so counsel can rely on them in Florida and foreign proceedings.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Florida licence for work in Miami?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Chapter 493, Florida Statutes, requires private investigative agencies to hold a Class A licence and investigators a Class C licence from the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. Attorneys in the regular practice of law are exempt. TDSC does not hold a Florida licence and coordinates Florida-licensed professionals for any local work.

faqs.q: How do you trace the owner of a Miami condominium held by an LLC?
faqs.a: Recorded deeds and mortgages usually name the entity, not the people behind it. We review Florida entity filings, foreign registrations, property tax and recording data, litigation, and connected entities in other countries. Where public sources do not establish ownership, counsel may be able to obtain disclosure through discovery or other legal process.

faqs.q: Can conversations be recorded in Florida?
faqs.a: Florida generally requires the consent of all parties before a private conversation is recorded, and covert recording can be a criminal offence. We plan interviews with counsel so that consent is obtained or recording is not used, and we do not undertake covert recording of private conversations in Florida.

faqs.q: Can you research Latin American owners behind a Miami company?
faqs.a: Yes, within lawful limits. We connect the Florida company to registries, court records, official gazettes and media in the relevant countries, working in Spanish and Portuguese. Where local fieldwork is needed abroad, we coordinate qualified and appropriately licensed local professionals. We screen each matter for US sanctions issues before accepting it.

faqs.q: Where are business disputes heard in Miami?
faqs.a: State disputes are heard in the Circuit Court of the Eleventh Judicial Circuit, which has a complex business litigation section for larger commercial cases. Federal cases are heard in the Southern District of Florida. Miami is also a common seat for international arbitration. Counsel chooses the forum and we tailor research to its rules.
